assignments.title: 26.7 Primary Source Report: The Declaration of Israel and the Language of Rights
assignments.html:
PRIMARY SOURCE REPORT
The Declaration of Israel and the Language of Rights
A document of 1948 read alongside the end of empires.
Report · 16 points · Word document upload
⚑ ─ ⚑ ─ ⚑
HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then write your report in Word and submit it as the submission box below describes.
THE TASK

Write a report of 450 to 650 words in Word. Answer all four questions below, in order, each under its own heading. Use the excerpt from the Declaration of the Establishment of the State of Israel and “Suez, Nasser, and the Arab-Israeli Wars”, and where a question asks for it, “India, Algeria, and the Rights of Man Turned Against Empire”. Put short quotations in quotation marks and cite each one in a footnote.

This subject involves peoples who suffered and who still disagree. Write plainly, carefully, and with respect. State the facts as the sources give them, and do not add details you have not read. You will be graded on the quality of your argument, not on which side you take.

YOUR REPORT

1. Read the Declaration excerpt. It rests the claim to a state on two grounds, one old and one new. Name them in your own words. Which did the writers expect to persuade the world, and what in the text or in “Suez, Nasser, and the Arab-Israeli Wars” leads you to think so?

2. The Declaration promises “complete equality of social and political rights to all its inhabitants” and appeals to the Arab inhabitants to take part in the new state. “Suez, Nasser, and the Arab-Israeli Wars” says that about seven hundred thousand Arabs left or were driven from their homes in the war, and that historians still argue over the causes. Use both to say what the Declaration can show a historian and what it cannot.

3. This week asks whether the rights of man were a gift of empire or a weapon against it. Choose one case, either Israel’s Declaration or India or Algeria from “India, Algeria, and the Rights of Man Turned Against Empire”, and argue which answer it supports. Give two pieces of evidence from the sources and lessons, and say what a person on the other side would point to.

4. Suppose that in November 1956 President Eisenhower had not opposed Britain and France, and that their landing had taken the whole Suez Canal. Using “Suez, Nasser, and the Arab-Israeli Wars”, say what might have followed for Nasser, for the Arab world, and between the superpowers, and what you think would have been gained or lost. Then say what you cannot know.

CriteriaExcellent (4)Proficient (3)Developing (2)Beginning (1)

SUBMISSION

Write your report in Word and save it to your OneDrive folder. Then open this assignment in Canvas, choose the OneDrive tab, select your file, and submit.

Your teacher will read your report and score it with the rubric above.

MODULE INTRODUCTION
Module Introduction: The End of Empires
Survey · 3 questions · not graded
⚑ ─ ⚑ ─ ⚑
Before you start

Welcome to The End of Empires. Answer the questions below before you open the first lesson. Your answers help your teacher see where the class is starting. This survey is not graded.

This module's goals:
  • Compare how India and Algeria won independence and what each outcome cost.
  • Describe the founding of Israel, the Suez Crisis, and the Arab-Israeli wars.
  • Weigh whether the language of rights served empires as a gift or their subjects as a weapon.

discussions.title: 26.8 Discussion: Gift or weapon?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Gift or weapon?
Did the rights of man come with empire, or were they turned against it?
Graded discussion · 10 points · one post and one reply
⚑ ─ ⚑ ─ ⚑
HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then post your answer to the prompt below, and reply to one classmate.
DISCUSSION PROMPT

This week’s question: Were the rights of man a gift of empire or a weapon against it?

Choose one answer. Use your two-column list. Name two cases, such as India, Algeria, Vietnam, or Israel, and give one piece of evidence from each that supports your answer. Then name one case or fact that fits the other side of your list, and say why it does not change your mind.

Write 150 to 250 words. State one claim you believe is true. Then explain why, using the specific evidence named above. Write plainly and with respect, especially about the wars and the people who suffered in them. Keep to what the lessons and the sources show. If you are guessing, say so.

Then add one sentence on honesty. Did the rulers live up to the words about rights that they used in public? Name one case and say why.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a fact or decision they did not use. If not, say politely where you think it falls short, and give your reason.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
CriteriaSubstantive (full credit)Thin (partial credit)Missing (no credit)
Your claim and your reasons
